claim: DTX3L expands the non-proteinaceous substrate repertoire to include single-stranded DNA and RNA.
source: Here, we show that the DELTEX family member DTX3L expands this non-proteinaceous substrate repertoire to include single-stranded DNA and RNA.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1F and 1G demonstrating ubiquitination of ssDNA and ssRNA oligonucleotides.

claim: The minimal catalytically competent fragment of DTX3L comprises the C-terminal RING and DTC domains (RD).
source: Although the N-terminal region of DTX3L contains single-stranded nucleic acid binding domains and motifs, the minimal catalytically competent fragment comprises the C-terminal RING and DTC domains (RD).
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1H and 1I showing that DTX3L-RD is sufficient to catalyze ubiquitination of ssDNA and ssRNA, while RING or DTC alone are not.

claim: DTX3L-RD catalyses ubiquitination of the 3'-end of single-stranded DNA and RNA.
source: DTX3L-RD catalyses ubiquitination of the 3'-end of single-stranded DNA and RNA, as well as double-stranded DNA with a 3' overhang of two or more nucleotides.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2F showing that 3'-end labeling blocks ubiquitination, and Figure 2I showing that 3' phosphate modification prevents ubiquitination.

claim: DTX3L-RD catalyses ubiquitination of double-stranded DNA with a 3' overhang of two or more nucleotides.
source: DTX3L-RD catalyses ubiquitination of the 3'-end of single-stranded DNA and RNA, as well as double-stranded DNA with a 3' overhang of two or more nucleotides.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 3E showing that dsDNA with 2 or 3 nucleotide overhangs can be ubiquitinated, but not dsDNA with 1 nucleotide overhang.

claim: The ubiquitination modification of nucleic acids by DTX3L is reversibly cleaved by deubiquitinases.
source: This modification is reversibly cleaved by deubiquitinases.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 2C and 2D showing that USP2 treatment removes the Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA bands.

claim: The DTC domain binds single-stranded DNA.
source: NMR and biochemical analyses reveal that the DTC domain binds single-stranded DNA and facilitates the catalysis of Ub transfer from RING-bound E2-conjugated Ub.
evidence: This is supported by NMR data in Figure 4A-C showing chemical shift perturbations upon ssDNA binding, and competition assays in Figure 4D.

claim: The DTC domain facilitates the catalysis of Ub transfer from RING-bound E2-conjugated Ub.
source: NMR and biochemical analyses reveal that the DTC domain binds single-stranded DNA and facilitates the catalysis of Ub transfer from RING-bound E2-conjugated Ub.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement of both RING and DTC domains for activity (Figure 1H-I) and the catalytic residue mutations (Figure 4I).

claim: Ubiquitination typically involves covalent linking of ubiquitin to a lysine residue on a protein substrate.
source: Ubiquitination typically involves covalent linking of ubiquitin (Ub) to a lysine residue on a protein substrate.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: Non-lysine ubiquitination of protein substrates via serine residues has been demonstrated.
source: Non-lysine ubiquitination of protein substrates via serine (Wang et al., 2009) and threonine (Shimizu et al., 2010) residues has also been demonstrated.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Non-lysine ubiquitination of protein substrates via threonine residues has been demonstrated.
source: Non-lysine ubiquitination of protein substrates via serine (Wang et al., 2009) and threonine (Shimizu et al., 2010) residues has also been demonstrated.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The modification of serine and threonine residues produces an ester linkage in contrast to the canonical isopeptide amide bond observed in ubiquitination of lysine residues.
source: The modification of these residues produces an ester linkage in contrast to the canonical isopeptide amide bond that is observed in the ubiquitination of lysine residues (Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide is ubiquitinated by RNF213 in the immune response to Salmonella.
source: These substrates include bacterial lipopolysaccharide which is ubiquitinated by RNF213 in the immune response to Salmonella (Otten et al., 2021)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Glucosaccharides are ubiquitinated by HOIL-1.
source: glucosaccharides which are ubiquitinated by HOIL-1 (Kelsall et al., 2022)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Adenosine 5′-diphosphate (ADP)–ribose (ADPr) is ubiquitinated by the DELTEX family of ubiquitin ligases.
source: adenosine 5′-diphosphate (ADP)–ribose (ADPr) which is ubiquitinated by the DELTEX family of ubiquitin ligases (E3s) (Chatrin et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The DELTEX (DTX) E3 family is comprised of five RING E3s: DTX1, DTX2, DTX3, DTX3L, and DTX4.
source: The DELTEX (DTX) E3 family is comprised of five RING E3s, DTX1, DTX2, DTX3, DTX3L, and DTX4, which share a conserved C-terminal region containing the RING and DELTEX C-terminal (DTC) domains (Chatrin et al., 2020; Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: DTX family members share a conserved C-terminal region containing the RING and DELTEX C-terminal (DTC) domains.
source: The DELTEX (DTX) E3 family is comprised of five RING E3s, DTX1, DTX2, DTX3, DTX3L, and DTX4, which share a conserved C-terminal region containing the RING and DELTEX C-terminal (DTC) domains (Chatrin et al., 2020; Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The RING domain functions by recruiting E2 thioesterified with Ub (E2~Ub) to catalyse Ub transfer to a substrate.
source: Whilst the RING domain functions by recruiting E2 thioesterified with Ub (E2~Ub) to catalyse Ub transfer to a substrate (Deshaies and Joazeiro, 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: DTX3L forms a heterodimer with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 9 (PARP9).
source: DTX3L, which forms a heterodimer with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 9 (PARP9) (Takeyama et al., 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: DTX3L was initially proposed to be an activator of PARP9 ADP-ribosyltransferase activity.
source: DTX3L, which forms a heterodimer with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 9 (PARP9) (Takeyama et al., 2003), was initially proposed to be an activator of PARP9 ADP-ribosyltransferase activity
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The DTX3L/PARP9 complex was shown to catalyse ADP-ribosylation of Ub in the presence of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and ubiquitination components including E1, E2, Ub, Mg2+, and ATP.
source: with the complex being shown to catalyse ADP-ribosylation of Ub in the presence of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and ubiquitination components including E1, E2, Ub, Mg2+, and ATP (Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: It was originally proposed that PARP9 was responsible for ADP-ribosylation activity, despite previous reports of its catalytic inactivity.
source: It was originally proposed that PARP9 was responsible for this activity, despite previous reports of its catalytic inactivity (Vyas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: DTX3L tested independently of PARP9 was sufficient to catalyse ADP-ribosylation of the C-terminus of Ub.
source: When we tested DTX3L independently of PARP9, it was sufficient to catalyse ADP-ribosylation of the C-terminus of Ub (Chatrin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: The C-terminal RING and DTC domains (RD domains) are the minimal fragments required to catalyse ADP-ribosylation of Ub and all members of the DTX family share this capability.
source: Notably, the C-terminal RING and DTC domains (hereafter referred to as RD domains) are the minimal fragments required to catalyse this reaction and all members of the DTX family share this capability (Chatrin et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The DTC domain contains a pocket that binds ADPr and NAD+.
source: Structural analyses of RD domains revealed that the DTC domain contains a pocket that binds ADPr and NAD+ (Chatrin et al., 2020; Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: RD domains recruit ADPr-modified substrates and catalyse their ubiquitination in a poly-ADP-ribose (PAR)-dependent manner.
source: This enables RD domains to recruit ADPr-modified substrates and catalyse their ubiquitination in a poly-ADP-ribose (PAR)-dependent manner (Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In the presence of NAD+ and ubiquitination components, RD domains catalyse ADP-ribosylation of Ub.
source: In addition, in the presence of NAD+ and ubiquitination components, RD domains catalyse ADP-ribosylation of Ub (Chatrin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The chemical linkage of ADP-ribosylated Ub occurs between the carboxylate group of Ub Gly76 and the 3'-hydroxyl group of the adenosine-proximal ribose of ADPr or NAD+.
source: The chemical linkage of ADP-ribosylated Ub was recently discovered to occur between the carboxylate group of Ub Gly76 and the 3'-hydroxyl group of the adenosine-proximal ribose of ADPr or NAD+, highlighting Ub modification of ADPr or NAD+ rather than the canonical ADP-ribosylation of substrate that involves the release of nicotinamide from NAD+ followed by attachment of ADPr via the C1 atom of the nicotinamide ribose (Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The RD domains of both DTX2 and DTX3L can ubiquitinate the 3'-hydroxyl group of the adenosine-proximal ribose of free ADPr.
source: Furthermore, recent studies have demonstrated that the RD domains of both DTX2 and DTX3L can ubiquitinate the 3'-hydroxyl group of the adenosine-proximal ribose of free ADPr as well as ADPr moieties present on ADP-ribosylated proteins (Zhu et al., 2022) and ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids (Zhu et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The RD domains of both DTX2 and DTX3L can ubiquitinate ADPr moieties present on ADP-ribosylated proteins.
source: Furthermore, recent studies have demonstrated that the RD domains of both DTX2 and DTX3L can ubiquitinate the 3'-hydroxyl group of the adenosine-proximal ribose of free ADPr as well as ADPr moieties present on ADP-ribosylated proteins (Zhu et al., 2022) and ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids (Zhu et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The RD domains of both DTX2 and DTX3L can ubiquitinate ADPr moieties present on ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids.
source: Furthermore, recent studies have demonstrated that the RD domains of both DTX2 and DTX3L can ubiquitinate the 3'-hydroxyl group of the adenosine-proximal ribose of free ADPr as well as ADPr moieties present on ADP-ribosylated proteins (Zhu et al., 2022) and ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids (Zhu et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DTX3L has a unique N-terminus lacking the WWE domains and proline-rich regions found in the other DTX family members.
source: DTX3L has a unique N-terminus lacking the WWE domains and proline-rich regions found in the other DTX family members.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about DTX3L structure.

claim: The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database has allowed the prediction of unsolved protein structures to a higher degree of confidence than previously possible.
source: The development of the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (Jumper et al., 2021) has allowed the prediction of unsolved protein structures to a higher degree of confidence than previously possible.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the AlphaFold publication.

claim: AlphaFold allowed the generation of a model of DTX3L that revealed putative domains in the N-terminal region.
source: For DTX3L, this allowed the generation of a model of the protein that revealed putative domains in the N-terminal region.
evidence: This is based on computational prediction using AlphaFold.

claim: When queried in the DALI server, DTX3L domains were found to be structurally similar to K Homology (KH) domains and RNA recognition motifs (RRMs) which bind single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) and RNA (ssRNA).
source: When queried in the DALI server, which enables protein structures to be compared in 3D, these domains were found to be structurally similar to K Homology (KH) domains and RNA recognition motifs (RRMs) which bind single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) and RNA (ssRNA).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison using DALI server and known binding properties of KH domains and RRMs.

claim: DTX3L was able to bind a variety of sequences of ssDNA and ssRNA.
source: Here, we showed that DTX3L was able to bind a variety of sequences of ssDNA and ssRNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 1D and 1E.

claim: DTX3L was able to ubiquitinate ssDNA and ssRNA.
source: Unexpectedly, we discovered that DTX3L was able to ubiquitinate ssDNA and ssRNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by gel-based ubiquitination assays in Figure 1F and 1G.

claim: Several of the AlphaFold-predicted domains of DTX3L share structural similarities to KH domains.
source: Several of these domains share structural similarities to KH domains (Figure 1B and C)
evidence: This is shown by structural overlay in Figure 1B and C comparing DTX3L domains to known KH domains.

claim: The N-terminal domain of DTX3L resembles an RRM.
source: with the N-terminal domain resembling an RRM.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison using AlphaFold prediction.

claim: KH domains bind both ssRNA and ssDNA.
source: KH domains, which bind both ssRNA (Baber et al., 1999) and ssDNA (Baber et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: KH domains comprise a three-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet packed alongside three α-helices.
source: KH domains, which bind both ssRNA (Baber et al., 1999) and ssDNA (Baber et al., 2000), comprise a three-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet packed alongside three α-helices
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about KH domains.

claim: RRMs are composed of two α-helices and four anti-parallel strands packed together in a β-α-β-β-α-β fold.
source: whereas RRMs are composed of two α-helices and four anti-parallel strands packed together in a β-α-β-β-α-β fold (Cléry et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about RRMs supported by citation.

claim: Both full-length DTX3L and DTX3L 232-C construct bound to all tested sequences of ssRNA and ssDNA, inducing at least a twofold change in polarisation.
source: Both DTX3L constructs bound to all tested sequences of ssRNA and ssDNA, inducing at least a twofold change in polarisation (Figure 1D and E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence polarization data in the cited figures.

claim: At least a twofold change in polarisation was observed when DTX3L-PARP9 complex binding was tested with ssDNA and ssRNA, demonstrating that PARP9 does not occlude ssDNA or ssRNA binding by DTX3L.
source: Likewise, at least a twofold change in polarisation was observed when DTX3L-PARP9 complex binding was tested with these nucleic acids, demonstrating that PARP9 does not occlude ssDNA or ssRNA binding by DTX3L (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence polarization data and interpreted to mean PARP9 does not block binding.

claim: The appearance of an ~15 kDa band closely matched the combined molecular weights of Ub (8564 Da) and 20 nt FAM-labelled single-stranded nucleic acid (~6900–7300 Da), suggesting that both ssDNA and ssRNA were ubiquitinated by DTX3L.
source: The appearance of an ~15 kDa band closely matched the combined molecular weights of Ub (8564 Da) and 20 nt FAM-labelled single-stranded nucleic acid (~6900–7300 Da), suggesting that both ssDNA (Figure 1F) and ssRNA (Figure 1G) were ubiquitinated by DTX3L.
evidence: This is based on molecular weight calculation and gel data showing the band.

claim: DTX3L 232-C exhibited reduced autoubiquitination compared to DTX3L FL.
source: While DTX3L 232-C exhibited reduced autoubiquitination compared to DTX3L FL (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G)
evidence: This is shown by autoubiquitination assay data in the cited figure.

claim: The rates of UBE2D2~Ub discharge were comparable between DTX3L 232-C and DTX3L FL.
source: the rates of UBE2D2~Ub discharge were comparable (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is shown by lysine discharge assay data in the cited figure.

claim: DTX3L 232-C is as catalytically competent as DTX3L FL, but lacks accessible lysine sites necessary for autoubiquitination.
source: This suggests that DTX3L 232-C is as catalytically competent as DTX3L FL, but lacks accessible lysine sites necessary for autoubiquitination.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparable discharge rates but reduced autoubiquitination.

claim: DTX3L 232-C exhibited similar activity as DTX3L FL in catalysing the formation of Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA.
source: DTX3L 232-C exhibited similar activity as DTX3L FL in catalysing the formation of Ub-DNA (Figure 1H) and Ub-RNA (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data in the cited figures.

claim: DTX3L-RD catalysed the formation of Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA, whereas neither the RING (R) nor the DTC (D) alone sufficed.
source: DTX3L-RD also catalysed the formation of Ub-DNA (Figure 1H) and Ub-RNA (Figure 1I), whereas neither the RING (R) nor the DTC (D) alone sufficed.
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data comparing different domain constructs in the cited figures.

claim: The formation of Ub-DNA is time-dependent.
source: We took advantage of the Coomassie staining method of detection for Ub-DNA, along with an increased concentration of D4, to confirm this and demonstrate that the formation of Ub-DNA is time-dependent (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is shown by time-course data in Figure 1J.

claim: An ~15 kDa band corresponding to the predicted molecular weight of Ub-DNA was observed using ssDNA with IRDye 800 label and unlabelled ssDNA.
source: An ~15 kDa band corresponding to the predicted molecular weight of Ub-DNA was also observed using ssDNA with the alternative label (Figure 1K) and unlabelled ssDNA (Figure 1L).
evidence: This is shown by gel data in the cited figures demonstrating ubiquitination with different labels.

claim: DTX3L binds and ubiquitinates ssNAs and DTX3L-RD is the minimal fragment required to catalyse this reaction.
source: Together, our data demonstrate that DTX3L binds and ubiquitinates ssNAs and that DTX3L-RD is the minimal fragment required to catalyse this reaction.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the binding and ubiquitination data presented.

claim: Formation of Ub-DNA or Ub-RNA by DTX3L-RD was only detected when all components of the ubiquitination cascade (E1, UBE2D2, Ub, Mg2+-ATP) were present.
source: Formation of Ub-DNA or Ub-RNA by DTX3L-RD was only detected when all components of the ubiquitination cascade (E1, UBE2D2, Ub, Mg2+-ATP) were present (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is shown by component omission experiments in the cited figures.

claim: The ~15 kDa band disappeared upon treatment with USP2, which is consistent with the removal of Ub from ssDNA and ssRNA and shows that this modification is reversible.
source: The ~15 kDa band disappeared upon treatment with USP2, which is consistent with the removal of Ub from ssDNA (Figure 2C) and ssRNA (Figure 2D) and shows that this modification is reversible.
evidence: This is shown by USP2 treatment data in the cited figures.

claim: Treatment of Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA with Benzonase caused the disappearance of both the Ub-DNA and DNA bands and Ub-RNA and RNA bands.
source: Treatment of Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA with Benzonase, an endonuclease which degrades DNA and RNA, caused the disappearance of both the Ub-DNA and DNA bands (Figure 2C) and Ub-RNA and RNA bands (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown by Benzonase treatment data in the cited figures.

claim: Poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG) was recently shown to cleave Ub-ADPr attached to nucleic acid substrates.
source: Poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG), an ADPr hydrolase that cleaves ADPr-linked to substrate, was recently shown to cleave Ub-ADPr attached to a nucleic acid substrates (Zhu et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Treatment with PARG had no effect on the Ub-DNA band or Ub-RNA band, thereby demonstrating that this reaction is distinct from the attachment of Ub to the ADPr moiety on ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids.
source: Treatment with PARG had no effect on the Ub-DNA band (Figure 2C) or Ub-RNA band (Figure 2D), thereby demonstrating that this reaction is distinct from the attachment of Ub to the ADPr moiety on ADP-ribosylated nucleic acids (Zhu et al., 2024).
evidence: This is shown by PARG treatment data in the cited figures and interpreted to distinguish from ADPr-mediated ubiquitination.

claim: The 15 kDa product was ubiquitinated ssNAs.
source: These findings showed that the 15 kDa product was ubiquitinated ssNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the molecular weight, component requirements, and enzyme treatment data.

claim: DTX3L-RD did not ubiquitinate dsDNA suggesting that the protein is specific for ssDNA.
source: DTX3L-RD did not ubiquitinate dsDNA (D12, Table 1; Figure 2E) suggesting that the protein is specific for ssDNA.
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data with dsDNA in the cited figure.

claim: The 6-FAM label on the 3'-end blocked ubiquitination of ssDNA.
source: We then compared ubiquitination of ssDNA labelled with 6-FAM on the 5'-end or 3'-end (D13, Table 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, L) and found that the 6-FAM label on the 3'-end blocked ubiquitination of ssDNA (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is shown by comparing ubiquitination of 5' vs 3' labeled DNA in the cited figure.

claim: Treatment with pH 9.5 buffer led to the disappearance of the Ub-DNA band over time.
source: To see if the bond was hydrolysed under basic conditions, we treated our reaction with pH 9.5 buffer which led to the disappearance of the Ub-DNA band over time (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is shown by pH treatment data in the cited figure.

claim: Treatment with NH2OH resulted in the rapid disappearance of the Ub-DNA band.
source: Additionally, treatment with NH2OH resulted in the rapid disappearance of the Ub-DNA band (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is shown by hydroxylamine treatment data in the cited figure.

claim: The linkage between Ub and ssDNA is likely to be an ester.
source: Together, this suggested that the linkage is likely to be an ester, and that the modification occurs on a ribose moiety, leaving only the 3' ribose as a viable modification site.
evidence: This is inferred from the base and hydroxylamine lability data.

claim: ssDNA with a fluorine atom attached at the 2' position of the ribose ring was ubiquitinated.
source: Whilst ssDNA with a fluorine atom attached at the 2' position of the ribose ring (D14) was ubiquitinated, the addition of a phosphate moiety to the 3' hydroxyl of the ribose ring (D15) ablated the formation of Ub-DNA, thereby confirming this is the site of modification (D10, D14-D15, Table 1; Figure 2I).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data with modified nucleotides in the cited figure.

claim: The addition of a phosphate moiety to the 3' hydroxyl of the ribose ring ablated the formation of Ub-DNA, thereby confirming this is the site of modification.
source: Whilst ssDNA with a fluorine atom attached at the 2' position of the ribose ring (D14) was ubiquitinated, the addition of a phosphate moiety to the 3' hydroxyl of the ribose ring (D15) ablated the formation of Ub-DNA, thereby confirming this is the site of modification (D10, D14-D15, Table 1; Figure 2I).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data with modified nucleotides in the cited figure.

claim: The site of Ub modification of ssDNA is consistent with the site of Ub modification of ADPr where Ub is also attached to the 3' hydroxyl of the adenine-proximal ribose.
source: This is consistent with the site of Ub modification of ADPr where Ub is also attached to the 3' hydroxyl of the adenine-proximal ribose (Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a comparison to previously published data on ADPr modification.

claim: Ub modification of ssDNA occurs at the 3' hydroxyl of the 3' nucleotide.
source: These data support that Ub modification of ssDNA occurs at the 3' hydroxyl of the 3' nucleotide.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the 3' labeling and 3' phosphate modification experiments.

claim: Only the sequences ending with A and to some extent with G could be ubiquitinated by DTX3L-RD.
source: Whilst only the sequences ending with A and to some extent with G could be ubiquitinated by DTX3L-RD, the requirement for the penultimate nucleotide was less strict, with sequences ending CA, TA, and AA all being ubiquitinated (D16-D21, Table 1; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assays with different terminal nucleotides in the cited figures.

claim: The requirement for the penultimate nucleotide was less strict, with sequences ending CA, TA, and AA all being ubiquitinated.
source: Whilst only the sequences ending with A and to some extent with G could be ubiquitinated by DTX3L-RD, the requirement for the penultimate nucleotide was less strict, with sequences ending CA, TA, and AA all being ubiquitinated (D16-D21, Table 1; Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assays with different penultimate nucleotides in the cited figures.

claim: All four ssDNA nucleotides with the CAA repeat unit and ranging in length from five to 80 nucleotides were ubiquitinated.
source: When tested in our assays, all four of these nucleotide substrates were ubiquitinated (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assays with different length oligonucleotides in the cited figures.

claim: dsDNA with a single 3' nucleotide overhang could not be ubiquitinated.
source: Whilst dsDNA with a single 3' nucleotide overhang could not be ubiquitinated, dsDNA with a two or three 3' nucleotide overhang could be modified with Ub (D26-D29, Table 1; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assays with dsDNA with different overhang lengths in the cited figure.

claim: dsDNA with a two or three 3' nucleotide overhang could be modified with Ub.
source: Whilst dsDNA with a single 3' nucleotide overhang could not be ubiquitinated, dsDNA with a two or three 3' nucleotide overhang could be modified with Ub (D26-D29, Table 1; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assays with dsDNA with different overhang lengths in the cited figure.

claim: DTX3L modification of DNA requires that the two nucleotides at the 3' end be single-stranded.
source: Our data show that DTX3L modification of DNA requires that the two nucleotides at the 3' end be single-stranded.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the dsDNA overhang experiments.

claim: DTX3L-RD can ubiquitinate ssDNA of varying lengths and specific 3' dinucleotides.
source: Overall, these data demonstrate the ability of DTX3L-RD to ubiquitinate ssDNA of varying lengths and specific 3' dinucleotides.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the sequence and length variation experiments.

claim: Upon titration of ADPr or 5-nucleotide ssDNA, chemical shift perturbations (CSPs) occurred, indicating DTX3L-RD binds both ADPr and ssDNA.
source: Upon titration of ADPr or 5-nucleotide ssDNA, chemical shift perturbations (CSPs) occurred, indicating DTX3L-RD binds both ADPr and ssDNA (Figure 4A; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is shown by NMR data in the cited figures.

claim: The similarity in the CSPs indicates that there is some overlap in the binding sites of ADPr and ssDNA.
source: The similarity in the CSPs indicates that there is some overlap in the binding sites of ADPr and ssDNA (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is inferred from the similar NMR chemical shift patterns shown in the cited figures.

claim: The presence of ADPr inhibited the formation of Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA, suggesting they share the same binding site.
source: The presence of ADPr inhibited the formation of Ub-DNA and Ub-RNA (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), suggesting they share the same binding site.
evidence: This is shown by competition assay data in the cited figures.

claim: The addition of D31 inhibited the formation of Ub-NAD+.
source: The addition of D31 inhibited the formation of Ub-NAD+ (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is shown by competition assay data in the cited figure.

claim: D31 must be directly competing for binding because it has a phosphate moiety blocking the 3' hydroxyl ubiquitination site and cannot be ubiquitinated.
source: Because D31 has a phosphate moiety blocking the 3' hydroxyl ubiquitination site, it cannot be ubiquitinated; therefore, it must be directly competing for binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the structure of D31 and its inhibitory effect.

claim: DTX3L-RD displayed a kcat value of 0.0358±0.0034 min–1 and a Km value of 6.56±1.80 μM for Ub-D4 formation.
source: DTX3L-RD displayed a kcat value of 0.0358±0.0034 min–1 and a Km value of 6.56±1.80 μM for Ub-D4 formation, whereas the Michaelis-Menten curve did not reach saturation for Ub-F-NAD+ formation (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: This is shown by kinetic analysis data in the cited figures.

claim: The Michaelis-Menten curve did not reach saturation for Ub-F-NAD+ formation.
source: DTX3L-RD displayed a kcat value of 0.0358±0.0034 min–1 and a Km value of 6.56±1.80 μM for Ub-D4 formation, whereas the Michaelis-Menten curve did not reach saturation for Ub-F-NAD+ formation (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G).
evidence: This is shown by kinetic analysis data in the cited figures.

claim: DTX3L-RD exhibited 4.5-fold higher catalytic efficiency for D4 than F-NAD+.
source: Comparison of the estimated catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km = 5457 M–1 min–1 for D4 and estimated kcat/Km = 1190 M–1 min–1 for F-NAD+; Figure 4F) suggested that DTX3L-RD exhibited 4.5-fold higher catalytic efficiency for D4 than F-NAD+.
evidence: This is calculated from the kinetic data shown in the cited figure.

claim: This difference in catalytic efficiency primarily results from a better Km value for D4 compared to F-NAD+.
source: This difference primarily results from a better Km value for D4 compared to F-NAD+.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic parameters.

claim: DTX3L-RD displays a higher rate for converting F-NAD+ to Ub-F-NAD+ at higher substrate concentrations.
source: Although DTX3L-RD showed weak Km for F-NAD+, it displays a higher rate for converting F-NAD+ to Ub-F-NAD+ at higher substrate concentrations (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is shown by the kinetic curve in the cited figure.

claim: Substrate concentration will play a role in determining the preference between D4 and F-NAD+.
source: Thus, substrate concentration will play a role in determining the preference.
evidence: This is inferred from the kinetic behavior at different substrate concentrations.

claim: DTX2 His594 located in the DTC pocket is important for the interaction with ADPr.
source: Previously, we demonstrated the importance of DTX2 His594 located in the DTC pocket for the interaction with ADPr (Figure 4G; Ahmed et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and shown in the cited figure.

claim: The Y719A mutant of DTX3L was defective in the ubiquitination of ssDNA.
source: We examined the effect of mutating the corresponding residue (Tyr719) in DTX3L (Figure 4H) and found that the Y719A mutant was defective in the ubiquitination of ssDNA (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is shown by mutational analysis data in the cited figures.

claim: Two catalytic residues in the DTC domain of DTX2, His582 and Glu608, have been previously identified as important for the ubiquitination of ADPr, and are conserved across the DTX family members.
source: Two catalytic residues in the DTC domain of DTX2 (Zhu et al., 2022), His582 and Glu608, have been previously identified as important for the ubiquitination of ADPr, and are conserved across the DTX family members (Figure 4G and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and shown in the cited figures.

claim: Substitution of His707 by alanine in FL DTX3L completely abolished the formation of Ub-DNA.
source: Substitution of His707 by alanine in FL DTX3L completely abolished the formation of Ub-DNA, whilst substitution of Glu733 by alanine considerably impaired product formation (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is shown by mutational analysis data in the cited figure.

claim: Substitution of Glu733 by alanine considerably impaired Ub-DNA product formation.
source: Substitution of His707 by alanine in FL DTX3L completely abolished the formation of Ub-DNA, whilst substitution of Glu733 by alanine considerably impaired product formation (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is shown by mutational analysis data in the cited figure.

claim: The mechanism of ubiquitination is conserved across ssNAs, as shown by similar results with ssRNA R4 using mutant DTX3L.
source: To test whether this mechanism was conserved across ssNAs, we repeated the mutant DTX3L ubiquitination assay with ssRNA R4 and found similar results (Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is shown by mutational analysis data with ssRNA in the cited figure.

claim: DTX3L utilises the ADPr-binding pocket and the same catalytic residues in the DTC domain to bind and catalyse the ubiquitination of ssNAs.
source: Overall, the data support the idea that DTX3L utilises the ADPr-binding pocket and the same catalytic residues in the DTC domain to bind and catalyse the ubiquitination of ssNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the NMR, competition, and mutational data.

claim: Only DTX3L and to a lesser extent DTX3 were able to ubiquitinate ssDNA under the assay conditions.
source: Unexpectedly, only DTX3L and to a lesser extent DTX3 were able to ubiquitinate ssDNA under our assay conditions (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is shown by comparative ubiquitination assays with different DTX family members in the cited figures.

claim: No ubiquitination of ssDNA was observed even at a 10:1 molar ratio of DTC to RING domain, indicating that the ubiquitination of ssDNA only occurs at an appreciable rate in cis.
source: No ubiquitination of ssDNA was observed even at a 10:1 molar ratio of DTC to RING domain (Figure 5E), indicating that the ubiquitination of ssDNA only occurs at an appreciable rate in cis.
evidence: This is shown by trans-complementation experiment data in the cited figure.

claim: DTX2 was unable to ubiquitinate 9 different ssDNA sequences.
source: Next, we examined whether DTX2 could catalyse the ubiquitination of ssDNA using 9 different ssDNA sequences and found that DTX2 was unable to ubiquitinate them (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data in the cited figure.

claim: Both DTX2R-DTX3LD and DTX3LR-DTX2D chimeras were competent in performing ubiquitination of biotin-NAD+.
source: Both chimeras were competent in performing ubiquitination of biotin-NAD+ (Figure 5G)
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data in the cited figure.

claim: Both DTX2R-DTX3LD and DTX3LR-DTX2D chimeras were unable to produce Ub-DNA.
source: but were unable to produce Ub-DNA (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data in the cited figure.

claim: The specific arrangement of the RING and DTC domains in DTX3L is crucial in specifying Ub modification of ssDNA.
source: These results suggest that the specific arrangement of the RING and DTC domains in DTX3L is crucial in specifying Ub modification of ssDNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the chimera experiments showing that domain swapping abolishes ssDNA ubiquitination.

claim: The DTC domain binds ssNAs, the RING domain recruits E2~Ub, and the RD domains bring the thioester linked Ub into proximity with the 3' end of ssNA.
source: Taken together, we propose a mechanism for the ubiquitination of ssNAs by the DTX3L-RD domains (Figure 5I): the DTC domain binds ssNAs, the RING domain recruits E2~Ub, and the RD domains bring the thioester linked Ub into proximity with the 3' end of ssNA.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The catalytic residues in the DTC domain enable the covalent attachment of Ub to the 3' hydroxyl group on the 3'-end of ssNA.
source: This allows the catalytic residues in the DTC domain to enable the covalent attachment of Ub to the 3' hydroxyl group on the 3'-end of ssNA.
evidence: This is part of the proposed mechanism based on the mutational and chemical data.

claim: The substrates for the DTC domain include ADPr, NAD+, and ADPr-modified nucleic acids and proteins.
source: The substrates for the DTC domain also include ADPr, NAD+, and ADPr-modified nucleic acids and proteins.
evidence: This is based on previous studies and the current findings.

claim: The RING domains of DTX3L and DTX3 lack insertions found in DTX1, DTX2, and DTX4, making their RING domains appear smaller.
source: The RING domains of DTX3L and DTX3 lack insertions found in DTX1, DTX2, and DTX4, making their RING domains appear smaller (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is shown by sequence alignment and structural comparison in the cited figures.

claim: DTX3L and DTX3 lack an AR motif found near the DTC pocket.
source: Furthermore, DTX3L and DTX3 lack an AR motif found near the DTC pocket.
evidence: This is shown by sequence alignment in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The absence of the AR motif causes a slight conformational change near the DTC pocket, resulting in an extended β-strand and the loss of a bulge containing the arginine residue.
source: The absence of the AR motif causes a slight conformational change near the DTC pocket, resulting in an extended β-strand and the loss of a bulge containing the arginine residue (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,D, E).
evidence: This is shown by structural comparison in the cited figures.

claim: DTX3L has an extended groove adjacent to the DTC pocket that could accommodate one or more of the nucleotides 5' to the targeted terminal nucleotide.
source: Consequently, DTX3L has an extended groove adjacent to the DTC pocket that could accommodate one or more of the nucleotides 5' to the targeted terminal nucleotide.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural differences shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Replacing DTX2-RD's DTC domain with that of DTX3L produced a chimeric construct that was able to ubiquitinate NAD+ but not ssDNA.
source: Replacing DTX2-RD's DTC domain with that of DTX3L produced a chimeric construct that was able to ubiquitinate NAD+ but not ssDNA (Figure 5G and H)
evidence: This is shown by ubiquitination assay data with chimeric constructs in the cited figures.

claim: Additional factors beyond the catalytic residues and ssDNA binding properties of the DTC domain likely play a role in ubiquitination.
source: suggesting that additional factors beyond the catalytic residues and ssDNA binding properties of the DTC domain likely play a role in ubiquitination.
evidence: This is inferred from the chimera experiment results.

claim: The ubiquitination reaction only occurs in cis, pointing to the orientation of the RING relative to the DTC domain as an important feature in the formation of Ub-DNA.
source: Our findings show that this reaction only occurs in cis, pointing to the orientation of the RING relative to the DTC domain as an important feature in the formation of Ub-DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the trans-complementation and chimera experiments.

claim: KH domains typically contain a GXXG motif within the loop between the first and second α helix.
source: Typically, KH domains contain a GXXG motif within the loop between the first and second α helix (Grishin, 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge about KH domains supported by citation.

claim: Analysis of the sequence of the KHL domains in DTX3L shows these domains lack the GXXG motif.
source: However, analysis of the sequence of the KHL domains in DTX3L shows these domains lack this motif.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of DTX3L.

claim: Multiple studies have shown that mutation in the GXXG motif abolishes binding to nucleic acids.
source: Multiple studies have shown that mutation in this motif abolishes binding to nucleic acids (Hollingworth et al., 2012; Talwar et al., 2017; Yadav et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The DTX3L DTC domain binds nucleic acids.
source: Our findings show the DTX3L DTC domain binds nucleic acids
evidence: This is shown by NMR and biochemical data in Figure 4.

claim: The structure of the first KHL domain was recently reported and shown to form a tetrameric assembly.
source: Additionally, the structure of the first KHL domain was recently reported and shown to form a tetrameric assembly (Vela-Rodríguez et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent work.

claim: DTX3L 232-C, which lacks the first KHL domain and RRM, can still bind ssDNA and ssRNA.
source: Our analysis with DTX3L 232-C, which lacks the first KHL domain and RRM, indicates that it can still bind ssDNA and ssRNA.
evidence: This is shown by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: DTX3L forms a heterodimeric complex with PARP9, facilitating the direct ubiquitination of substrates such as H2B.
source: It forms a heterodimeric complex with PARP9, facilitating the direct ubiquitination of substrates such as H2B (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The DTX3L/PARP9 complex can recruit PARylated substrates, either through PARP9 macrodomains or DTX3L DTC domain, for direct substrate ubiquitination.
source: This complex can recruit PARylated substrates, either through PARP9 macrodomains (Zhang et al., 2015) or DTX3L DTC domain (Ahmed et al., 2020), for direct substrate ubiquitination.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: DTX3L can catalyse the transfer of Ub to NAD+ or ADPr.
source: Notably, it can catalyse the transfer of Ub to NAD+ or ADPr (Chatrin et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2017; Zhu et al., 2022)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: DTX3L can catalyse the transfer of Ub to ADPr moieties of PARylated substrates, encompassing both proteins and nucleic acids.
source: including ADPr moieties of PARylated substrates, encompassing both proteins and nucleic acids (Zhu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The DTX3L/PARP9 complex has a known involvement in DNA damage repair, utilising PARP9's macrodomains to recognise PAR and assist in complex recruitment to the damaged foci.
source: The DTX3L/PARP9 complex has a known involvement in DNA damage repair, utilising PARP9's macrodomains to recognise PAR and assist in complex recruitment to the damaged foci (Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: RNA itself contributes to DNA damage repair.
source: RNA itself contributes to DNA damage repair (Bader et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Expression of DTX3L/PARP9 complex is induced after viral infection.
source: Studies have shown that expression of DTX3L/PARP9 complex is induced after viral infection
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The DTX3L/PARP9 complex plays a role in antiviral defense mechanisms by ubiquitinating both host and viral proteins.
source: and the complex plays a role in antiviral defense mechanisms by ubiquitinating both host and viral proteins (Zhang et al., 2015; Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.
